newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end higher, buoyed by earnings news.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end higher, buoyed by earnings news.

text.p: Mexican shares closed with solid gains on Tuesday as strong earnings reports and sagging U.S. bond yields lured buyers into the bourse, analysts said.

"Second-quarter earnings have been good on the whole, with some contrasting cases.... A good sign is they reflect a recovery in the domestic market and in purchasing power, as in retailers," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy.
The leading IPC share index finished 85.31 points, or 1.81 percent, higher at 4,797.49.
Cifra SA's B shares were in demand after the retailer posted earnings Monday evening, dealers said. The stock climbed 56 centavos to close at 15.56 pesos at brisk trade.

Galvan said expected cuts in Mexican primary interest rates later in the day helped boost share prices, especially with the yield on U.S. 30-year Treasury bond at 6.38 percent -- close to its year-low -- in late trading.
"Long-bond yields are rock-bottom...and the bolsa is getting more and more competitive compared to the money market," he said.

Nine money-market traders surveyed by Reuters forecast that Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 18.01 percent, or 71 basis points less than at last week's auction.

Traders said the IPC, after reaching as high as 4,799.90 points, eased amid light profit-taking, especially notable on market heavyweight Cemex SA. The cement maker shed 5 centavos to close at 37.80 pesos.
Volume picked up from a sluggish start to reach a healthy 123.9 million shares traded, although dealers noted one cross-trade accounted for almost 18 million shares.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced decliners by 64 to 44, out of a total of 120 stocks traded.
